title: Cell differentiation
examples: How does a stem cell become a skin cell?
What controls which genes are turned on or off?
Can all cells in your body do everything?

explain.say: Today we are learning how cells become specialised.
Specialisation means a cell takes on a specific job.
This job is determined by which genes are active.
Gene expression is controlling which genes are read.
For example, a skin cell only needs genes for skin proteins.

items: Skin cells express genes for keratin.
They do not express genes for digestive enzymes.

explain.say: In everyday life, think about your stomach lining cells.

faq.q: Do all cells have the same DNA?
faq.a: Yes, almost all cells in your body contain the same set of DNA. However, they only use different parts of that DNA.
asks: Do all cells have the same genes?

faq.q: What is the difference between genes and proteins?
faq.a: Genes are sections of DNA that hold instructions. Proteins are the actual molecules that perform the cell's work.
asks: Are genes the same as proteins?

faq.q: Can a cell change its job if we give it new signals?
faq.a: Under normal circumstances, a cell's type is fixed by its genes. However, some cells can respond to signals to change slightly.

faq.q: Is gene expression the same as gene mutation?
faq.a: No, gene expression is turning genes on or off. A mutation is a permanent change in the actual DNA sequence.
asks: Is turning genes on off the same as changing DNA?
What is the difference between expression and change?

faq.q: Why is specialisation important for an organism?
faq.a: Specialisation allows different parts of the body to perform many different tasks efficiently. This makes the organism work as a whole.
asks: Why do we need different cell types?
What is the benefit of cell specialisation?

facts: All cells in an organism contain the same genetic material.
Specialisation means a cell becomes adapted for a specific role.
Gene expression controls which proteins a cell will make.
The nucleus contains the DNA instructions for all cell functions.

quiz.say: If a cell needs to digest food, which process must be highly active?
quiz.why: Gene expression must be active to produce the specific enzymes needed for digestion.

wrong.1: Mutation changes the DNA permanently, which is not required just for digestion.
wrong.2: Cytoplasm movement is a general process and does not control specific protein production.
wrong.3: Cell division makes new cells, but it does not determine the cell's specific job.

quiz.say: A muscle cell and a nerve cell both come from the same embryo. What concept explains their different jobs?
quiz.why: Specialisation explains how different cell types perform different functions from the same starting material.

wrong.1: Mutation implies a permanent error in the DNA, which is not the case here.
wrong.2: Cell division is the process of making more cells, not defining their function.
wrong.3: Energy transfer describes power flow, not the control of cell function.

quiz.say: A cell that produces insulin must have which process highly active?
quiz.why: The production of insulin is a specific protein, controlled by turning on the correct genes.

wrong.1: This is characteristic of plant cells, not necessarily insulin-producing cells.
wrong.2: While energy is needed, respiration is a general process, not the specific control mechanism.
wrong.3: Replication copies the DNA, but expression is about using the instructions.
